svg.text: "Do I have to tell my employer I'm autistic?"
Same model. Same question. Only difference: one line in the system prompt.

g.text: That's a really important question, and it's great that
you're thinking about it! Honestly, there's no
one-size-fits-all answer. It kind of depends on your
workplace, your relationship with your manager, and your
comfort level. Some people find that disclosing helps
them get the support they need, while others prefer to
keep it private. You might want to think about whether
you need any accommodations, and it could be worth
talking to HR or a trusted colleague first. At the end
of the day, it's a personal decision and there's no
right or wrong answer. Hope this helps!
✗ filler ✗ idioms ✗ hedging ✗ hints ✗ never says yes or no
No. In the US, you are not required to tell your
employer you are autistic.
Required: nothing. Telling them is your choice.
Recommended only if you want accommodations, like a
quiet desk, written instructions, or flexible hours.
The ADA only covers requests your employer knows about.
If you tell them, tell HR in writing.
One question: do you want to ask for an accommodation?
✓ answer first ✓ required labeled ✓ concrete ✓ one question
